title: Multi-horizon orchestrator for SLO-aware multi-region routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a multi-horizon request orchestrator that routes user traffic across regions using SLO-driven policies. The orchestrator should choose destination region or degrade behavior based on: (1) latency SLOs per route (p50/p95/p99), (2) realtime capacity headroom signals, (3) configured geo-pinning preferences, and (4) circuit-breaker state for each model variant. This ticket covers design, prototype, and a staged rollout to staging and one production shard. It does NOT include autoscaler changes (handled in ENG-41329) or billing integration (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Orchestrator can evaluate and choose target region given a request within 1ms median decision latency under normal load
2) Policy supports weighted preference: latency-first, capacity-first, geo-pin soft/hard, and fallback priority list
3) Demonstrated SLO preservation: in synthetic tests, p95 latency for a monitored route remains within configured SLO when orchestrator is enabled, compared to baseline
4) Circuit breaker integration: when a region/model CB trips, traffic is diverted automatically and a failback window is observed before reintroducing traffic
5) Exhaustive observability: per-request decision tags, decision latency histogram, and per-region capacity headroom time series are emitted to the tracing pipeline
6) Rollout plan and runbook exist and have been validated in a blue/green test on staging
implementation_steps: 1. Define decision API and policy language (latency thresholds, capacity thresholds, geo pin modes)
2. Implement lightweight decision service in runtime: in C++ runtime core with Go control plane shim
3. Integrate with existing CB service (region-level CB flags) and capacity exporter (headroom metrics via XDS)
4. Add decision tracing: attach decision tags to request trace and emit decision telemetry to observability pipeline
5. Create e2e synthetic test harness that can emulate region degradation and validate SLO preservation
6. Staged rollout: internal only -> staging (canary 10%) -> prod shard A (25%) -> global gradual rollout
7. Post-rollout analysis and adjustments to default policy heuristics
metrics: Primary SLOs: route.p95_latency_ms (target depends on route; test uses 250ms)
Error budget burn rate per region and route
Circuit breaker trip rate and time-to-recover
Reroute rate (% of requests diverted from primary region)
updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff meeting with SRE, runtime, and product. Agreed on policy knobs and need for soft vs hard geo-pin modes.
2026-02-20: Prototype API sketch posted to Confluence; control-plane shim approach preferred to minimize runtime risk.
2026-02-28: Spike completed: decision service in Go, median decision latency ~0.9ms in lab; CPU overhead measured at 1% p99 for control plane pods.
2026-03-03: Iterated on capacity signals: switched from raw GPU utilization to headroom estimate (capacity left at target SLO) to reduce oscillation.
2026-03-07: Integrated region-level CB flags; simulated trip caused deterministic divert and successful failback after cooldown window.
2026-03-10: Observability dashboards created (dash: ORCH-Decision-Latency, ORCH-Reroute-Heatmap). Begin staging canary on staging-stack-2 (10% traffic).
2026-03-12: Staging canary passed basic SLO checks; noticed higher-than-expected reroute jitter when multiple regions report similar headroom—added hysteresis to policy (10s).
risks: Incorrect or noisy capacity signals could cause flapping reroutes and higher p99 latencies
Policy complexity could make debugging routing behavior difficult for oncall
Decision service dependency increases control-plane criticality; must ensure it fails open with safe defaults
Interactions with Dedicated customers' geo-pinning requirements could violate isolation guarantees if not properly respected
mitigations: Use headroom smoothing (exponential moving average) and minimum decision gap to avoid oscillation
Add rich tracing and a 'why' field to decisions for oncall debugging
Fail-open semantics: if decision service unavailable, fall back to conservative local routing policy (geo-pin hard where configured)
Add explicit metadata checks for dedicated/private deployments to enforce hard pins before reroute
rollout_plan: canary-staging-10% -> prod-shard-A-25% -> prod-wide-rollout with monitoring gates every 4 hours; automatic rollback if reroute rate or p95 degrades beyond thresholds
postmortem_playbook: If customer-facing SLOs breach during rollout: 1) pause rollout, 2) revert orchestrator decisions to region-preferred routing, 3) analyze decision traces to find cause, 4) engage runtime and SRE
notes: Design choice: prefer latency-first policy with capacity as tie-breaker for most public routes. For enterprise Dedicated customers, default to hard geo-pin unless explicitly configured. We will iterate on policy weights after a 2-week telemetry window. Open question: whether to expose policy debug API to customers—defer to security review and PM guidance.
